findings.title: SiteSetting is consulted on every fallback translation lookup
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym every time I18n asks for the fallback chain, which happens during translation lookups rather than once per request. This adds a site-setting lookup (and potential cache/database work) to hot translation paths and also makes translation depend on SiteSetting being available; if default_locale is nil/blank during boot, migrations, or in a bare console/job context, to_sym on nil (or loading a blank locale) can break otherwise-valid translations. Compute/cache the site default safely (e.g. per request or with a nil/blank guard) instead of querying it inside the fallback map.

findings.title: Cached translations can permanently cache a missing-translation result before fallback locales are loaded
findings.body: translate() caches translate_no_cache(key) in the LRU under only key+locale+backend, but with fallbacks the result depends on whether the site-default and :en locale files have been loaded yet. If a key is first translated in the user locale before its fallback locales are loaded, I18n returns a 'translation missing' string and that string is frozen and cached; loading the fallback locale afterwards does not clear @cache (only reload! does), so users can keep seeing missing-translation text until restart/reload. The cache must be invalidated when load_locale loads a new locale, or translations must ensure all fallback locales are loaded before caching.

findings.title: Fallback locales are only ensured loaded for web requests
findings.body: I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is called only from ApplicationController#set_locale. Background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, and other code paths that set I18n.locale without going through this controller will translate with only config.locale loaded (translate_accelerator only auto-loads config.locale), so fallback lookups against the site default/:en can return missing translations instead of the English/site text. Move the ensure-loaded logic into the I18n translation/load path itself (or into every locale-setting entry point), not just the request cycle.

findings.title: FallbackLocaleList is a Hash in name only and drops configured fallback semantics
findings.body: I18n.fallbacks is normally an I18n::Locale::Fallbacks object that supports defaults, explicit per-locale mappings, and locale expansion (e.g. en_US -> en). Replacing it with a Hash subclass whose [] ignores any stored entries and always fabricates [locale, site_default, :en] means code or gems that assign/inspect fallbacks (I18n.fallbacks[:de] = [...], defaults, include?) silently lose those settings, and regional locales get no parent-language fallback (zh_TW never falls back to zh, pt_BR never to pt). Implement the fallback object API or subclass I18n::Locale::Fallbacks and override compute instead of faking a Hash.
